- When sentiment is consistently positive or rising, model tends to underreact — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean or spike magnitude.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots — cap forecast at +3–5% above peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment turns negative or shows strong downward momentum, model frequently lags — add 1–2 days of lagged negative sentiment adjustment to forecast.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- High news volume with low sentiment change suggests model overweights noise — dampen forecast by 0.5–1.5% per news unit.
- If sentiment change is negative and forecast is rising, reverse direction — model often misinterprets sentiment shift as bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates late-period volatility — add 0.5–1.5% buffer for final 5–7 days if sentiment is volatile or news is high.
